events.region: Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out 20 NM; Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM; Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20 Nm
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...

* Until 900 AM EDT/800 AM CDT/.

* At 701 AM EDT/601 AM CDT/, a severe thunderstorm capable of
producing waterspouts was located 9 nm southwest of Apalachicola,
moving west at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots...suddenly higher
waves...frequent lightning...and heavy downpours.
Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats and damage
vessels. Make sure all on board are in a secure location
and wearing life jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Cape San Blas.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Liberty, TX; Polk, TX; San Jacinto, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Northern Liberty County in southeastern Texas...
Southeastern Polk County in southeastern Texas...
East Central San Jacinto County in southeastern Texas...

* WHEN...Until 815 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding including FM 943 at Menard Creek near
Segno.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 600 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Between 6 and 16 inches of rain have fallen.
- Rainfall is beginning to filter back into Polk County. Additional
rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned
area. If rainfall persists for an extended period of time or if
rain rates increase, this may need to be upgraded to a Flash
Flood Warning again.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Shepherd, Goodrich, Alabama-Coushatta Reservation and Segno.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Neches River Near Diboll affecting Polk, Angelina and Trinity
Counties.

For the Neches River...including Neches, Alto, Diboll, Rockland...
Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River near Diboll.

* WHEN...From this evening to late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor lowland flooding occurs.  Expect
flooded boat ramps and trails.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:15 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 3.4 feet.
- Forecast...The Neches River south of Diboll is expected to rise
above flood stage this evening to a crest of 12.1 feet just after
midnight tonight. It will then fall below flood stage tomorrow
morning.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.1
feet on 05/21/1956.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
